concept.name: Volume point of control
concept.definition: The price level within a volume profile at which the greatest volume traded during the measured period — the highest-volume row of the histogram. It is the volume-based counterpart of the TPO point of control and is read as the price of maximum two-sided agreement by traded quantity.
concept.intuition: The VPOC is where the most contracts actually changed hands — the market's busiest price over the period.
concept.mechanics: After volume is binned into price rows, the row with the largest total volume is marked as the VPOC; many platforms also plot a developing VPOC line showing how the level migrated during the period.
concept.formula: VPOC = argmax over price rows p of V(p), where V(p) is total volume traded in row p over the profile period
concept.failure_modes: The VPOC shifts as the period develops and depends on the chosen range and row size; on uneven-volume days the volume POC and time-based (TPO) POC sit at different prices, and choosing between them is contextual.
concept.misconceptions: The VPOC is not a proven magnet for future price; retest reactions are a documented practitioner observation, not a reliable regularity, and expecting precise bounces off the level is flagged as a mistake by platform documentation.
concept.example: Over a two-week fixed-range profile, the most-traded row is 4,480 with 1.1M contracts; that VPOC is carried forward as a reference when price returns to the area.
